\title{Exogenous Predictors in Pooled Intraday Forecasts of Realized Variance\ifauthornotes\\\large Bullet-point
draft of the full paper\fi\\\large Review layer: top-level bullets only}
\author{James Chen \and Mihai Cucuringu \and Christopher S. Jones \and Austin Pollok}
\date{Working draft, 26 October 2026 --- not for citation}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
We ask what exogenous predictors, from constituents' trading to alternative data, add to pooled E-mini S\&P~500
realized-variance forecasts for every regular-hours half-hour bar. Against an OLS heterogeneous autoregressive (HAR)
benchmark, the full set lowers QLIKE loss significantly in all \rhorAfPairs{} model classes, by
\rhorVsOlsRedLinRng{}\% (penalized linear models) and \rhorVsOlsRedTreeRng{}\% (tree
ensembles), and beats augmented HAR models. The gain concentrates in the FOMC calendar and the futures' realized
moments; beyond them, only boosted trees gain, slightly. Under squared error, a few crash days offset it. In 0DTE
straddles, full-set forecasts beat passive selling but seldom significantly beat HAR forecasts.
\end{abstract}
